claim: For the Heawood graph, the point–line incidence graph of the binary Fano plane, a subset is a metric basis if and only if it consists of three noncollinear points and two of their three single-incidence tangent lines, or the point–line dual of such a subset. There are exactly 168 metric bases, 84 in each dual class. The graph whose vertices are these bases and whose edges are one-vertex replacements is connected, 5-regular on 168 vertices with 420 edges, and has radius and diameter 5. Every vertex has distance-layer profile (1,5,18,49,71,24). The bases partition into 56 disjoint triangles corresponding to the 28 noncollinear point triples and 28 nonconcurrent line triples; each basis has two within-triangle neighbors and three outside neighbors.
integrity_notes: Two separate standalone exact finite checkers, each with deterministic execution output; the self-review is not an independent audit.
scientific_limitations: Finite exhaustive classification for PG(2,2) only; no extension to other projective planes or token sliding. Previously known metric dimension 5 is explicitly not a new claim. Priority risks from unindexed or unpublished metric-basis-reconfiguration results remain.
title: Triangle–tangent metric bases and their exchange graph in the Heawood graph
